The informant Smt. Pavithra.V., filed private complaint against accused No.1 to 6 under Section 200 of Cr.P.C. for the offences punishable under Sec. 498(A), 323, 324, 342, 354, 504, 506 R/w Section Pavithra.V vs Ravichander on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143145740/

On receipt of complaint, the court registered the complaint as PCR and referred the case as required under Sec.156(3) of Cr.P.C. to R.T. Nagara Police Station for investigation and submit report.

Accordingly,
the Police Sub- Inspector of R.T. Nagara Police Station after the investigation, submitted charge sheet against accused No.1 to 6 for the offences punishable under Section 498(A), 323, 342, 504,
506 read with sec.149 of IPC arisen in Crime No.77/2021.
2.
Prosecution Case:
The marriage of CW1 namely Smt. Pavithra and the accused No.1 was solemnized on 22-04-2005 as per Hindu customs and rites.

After marriage, CW1 was residing at R.T.Nagara, Giddappa Block within the limits of R.T.Nagara Police Station, Bengaluru City with accused persons wherein the accused No.1 to 6 with common intention were subjected the CW1 to mental and physical cruelty.
Further, when accused No.1 brought his friends to his house, he would wrongfully confined CW1 in a room of house so that she would not talk to them.

On 05-04-2019 when CW1 returned from her work at 7 pm, the accused No.1 picked up quarrel with her and beaten her with his hands by suspecting her character and on next day i.e., on 06- 04-2019, the accused No.4 came to the house of CW1, abused her and threatened to throw acid on her.
3. First Information Report:

Upon the receipt of private complaint, CW6/PW2 namely Smt.
Jayashree Athani, the then WPSI of R.T. Nagara Police Station registered Crime No.77/2021 against accused for the offences punishable under Section 506, 498A, 504, 323, 324, 34 IPC and Sec.3, 4 of D P Act, prepared FIR as per Ex.P8 and sent the same to the Court and to his superior officers.

4. Investigation: Thereafter she drawn spot mahazar on 06-04-2021 as per Ex.P2 in the presence of CW4 namely Smt Kamarnaaz and CW5 Sri Javeed Khan from 8.30 am to 9.30 am, recorded the statement of witnesses, secured the photographs of CW1 as per Ex.P3 and 4 and submitted charge sheet against accused No.1 to 6 for the offences punishable under Section 498A, 323, 342, 504, 506 read with Sec. 149 of Indian Penal Code.
5.
The accused No.1 to 6 were enlarged on bail by the order dated 01-10-2021 6.

On receipt of charge sheet, this Court has taken cognizance for the offences alleged against the accused No.1 to 6.
7.

Copies of prosecution paper as required U/Sec.207 of Cr.P.C have been furnished to the accused No.1 to 6.
8.
Charge:

After hearing learned Senior APP and counsel for accused No.1 to 6, charge for the offences punishable under Section 498A, 323, 342, 504, 506, read with Sec.149 of Indian Penal Code has been framed, read over and explained to the accused No.1 to 6 in the language known to them, who, in turn, pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
9. Prosecution Evidence:
The prosecution in order to establish its case cited 6 witnesses, examined 2 witnesses and exhibited 9 documents and their side.

On account of settlement arrived between PW1 and accused No.1 in MC No.5940/2021, the examination of remaining witnesses is dispensed with Pavithra.V vs Ravichander on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143145740/
3 by the order dated 03- 10-2025.

10. Accused statement as per section 313 of CrPC: After completion of evidence of prosecution, the accused No.1 to 6 were examined as per section 313 of Cr.P.C, wherein they denied all incriminating evidence appearing in the statement of prosecution witnesses and did not lead any rebuttal evidence.
11. Heard the arguments.
Perused materials on the record.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on said duration and place,
with common object accused No.1 wrongfully confined CW1 in a room of house so that she would not talk to his friends when they visit his house thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable u/Sec.342 read with Sec.149 of IPC?
3. Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on 05-04-2019 and 06-04-2019, the accused No.1 and 4 abused CW1 with filthiest language, knowingly such abusive language will break the public peace thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable u/Sec.504 read with Sec.149 of IPC?
4.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on said duration and place,
with common object accused No.1 beaten CW1 with his hands and caused simple hurt to her thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable u/Sec.323 read with Sec.149 of IPC?
5.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on said date, place and time, in furtherance common intention, the accused No.1 threatened CW1 with dire consequences thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable u/Sec.506 read with Sec.149 of IPC?
6. What order?
13. The findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1-5 : In the Negative Point No.6 : As per final order REASONS 14. Point No.1 to 5: These points are taken up together for the purpose of common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts as they form the same part of transaction.

In support of prosecution case as narrated in paragraph 2 and the point for consideration in paragraph 12 of this Pavithra.V vs Ravichander on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143145740/
4 judgment, the prosecution examined the witnesses which are as follows (i) CW1 by name Smt Pavithra, being informant cum injured examined as PW1 deposed that she got married to the accused No.1 on 22-4- 2005 and that she gave Rs.2 lakh and gold ornaments to the accused.

After marriage, when she lived with the accused, they started ill-treating her, abused her by suspecting her character, accused No.1 beaten her and that the accused No.4 threatened her he would throw acid on her when he was drunken.
Hence, she along with accused No.1 moved to a separate house however the accused No.1 with the instigate of other accused persons, used to abuse her with filthiest language and used to beat her.
In May 2018, the accused picked up quarrel with her, attacked her with an iron rod, caused her blood injuries, took all her belongings and went to his mother's house.

Later, she filed a private complaint as Ex.P1, and the police said that she had been evicted as Ex.P2 and identified the 4 photographs related to the attack as Ex.P3 to 6.
(ii) CW6 by name Smt Jayashri Athin, the then WPSI of R.T.Nagar PS examined as PW2 deposed that PCR No.13352/2019 was received and a police case was registered, the first information report was submitted to the court as per Ex.P8, the marriage certificate and the injured photograph were obtained from CW1 and her further statement was recorded, the mahazar was drawn as per Ex.P2,
the statements of the witnesses were recorded, the investigation was completed and the charge sheet was filed against the accused.
15.
Evidence of Prosecution must be established that the accused persons subjected the PW1 to mental and physical cruelty.

Mere omnibus statement regarding harassment does not ipso facto makes out a case under section 498A IPC, prosecution is required to prove the overt acts attributed by the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt and the said principle is appreciated in case of Sakharam and another vs State of Maharastra reported in (2003) 12 SCC 368.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Basing this decision,
the present cases are taken up for discussion.
16. It is relevant to reiterate Section 498A of Indian Penal Code which reads as under Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty --

Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation.

-- For the purposes of this section, "cruelty" means-- (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.

Pavithra.V vs Ravichander on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143145740/
5

For commission of an offence under Section 498- A of IPC, the following necessary ingredients require to be satisfied:
(a) The woman must be married;
(b) She must be subjected to cruelty or harassment; and (c) Such cruelty or harassment must have been shown either by husband of the woman or by the relative of her husband and the said principle is appreciated in the case of U. Suvetha v. State reported in (2009) 6 SCC 757.
17.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Every harassment does not amount to "cruelty" within the meaning of Section 498-A.

For the purpose of Section 498-A, harassment simpliciter is not "cruelty" and it is only when harassment is committed for the purpose of coercing a woman or any other person related to her to meet an unlawful demand for property, etc. that it amounts to "cruelty" punishable under Section 498-A IPC and the said principle is appreciated in the case of State of A.P. vs. M. Madhusudhan Rao reported in (2008) 15 SCC 582.
18.

sentences.text: Cruelty can either be mental or physical.
It is difficult for straitjacket the term cruelty by means of a definition because cruelty is a relative term.

What constitutes cruelty for one person may not constitute cruelty for another person and the said principle is appreciated in the case of G.V.
Siddaramesh v. State of Karnataka reported in (2010) 3 SCC 152.

Thus, it appears from the cross examination of PW1 being material witness cum injured did not support the prosecution case for coherence with the contents of complaint and chief-in-examination on account of settlement arrived in matrimonial case between the PW1 and the accused No.1 .
20.
Mere production of Ex.P3 to Ex.P6 without any certificate as envisaged under Section 65 of Indian Evidence Act that the accused No.1 has beaten the PW1 on 05-04-2019.
No medical certificate was produced to corroborate her version as to the alleged assault 21.

In this case, PW2 being police personnel deposed about the lodging of complaint by the PW1 and then the post complaint procedure, however her evidence is formal in nature and only on the basis of her evidence without any corroborating evidence to the alleged incident, the accused No.1 to 6 cannot be held guilty for the alleged offences.

22. This court is of the opinion that even if other witnesses were examined by the prosecution and they supported the prosecution case that would not helpful as PW1 herself did not support the prosecution case in the cross examination.

This court has dispensed with the examination of other witnesses which could be only formal in nature and hence taken the prosecution evidence as closed after examination of police official witnesses.

At this stage, it is relevant to rely upon the decision in the case of Satish Mehra v. Delhi Administration and another reported in (1996) 9 SCC 766, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as follows:
"When the judge is fairly certain that there is no prospect of the case ending in conviction the valuable time of the court should not be wasted for holding a trial only for the purpose of formally completing the procedure to pronounce the conclusion on the future date."

sentences.text: By basing aforesaid principle by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the above case is applicable to this case as well.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the present case, it is clear that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubts.
Under these facts and circumstances of the case, the Point No.1 to 5 is answered in the negative.
23. Point No.6:-

In view of the above findings and reasons given on point No.1 to 5, this Court proceeds to pass the following:

In this case, PW2 being police personnel deposed about the lodging of complaint by the PW1 and then the post complaint procedure, however her evidence is formal in nature and only on the basis of her evidence without any corroborating evidence to the alleged incident, the accused No.1 to 6 cannot be held guilty for the alleged offences.
22. This court is of the opinion that even if other witnesses were examined by the prosecution and they supported the prosecution case that would not helpful as PW1 herself did not support the prosecution case in the cross examination.
This court has dispensed with the examination of other witnesses which could be only formal in nature and hence taken the prosecution evidence as closed after examination of police official witnesses.
At this stage, it is relevant to rely upon the decision in the case of Satish Mehra v. Delhi Administration and another reported in (1996) 9 SCC 766, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as follows:
"When the judge is fairly certain that there is no prospect of the case ending in conviction the valuable time of the court should not be wasted for holding a trial only for the purpose of formally completing the procedure to pronounce the conclusion on the future date."
Considering the facts and circumstances of the present case, it is clear that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubts.
